setup_notes: Fork main fast-forwarded to upstream 8f6c8300 and pushed. make test-race hit its 60m timeout while running the semantics/internal/* packages; those were then race-tested separately with go test -race ./semantics/... (all ok, no races). Every other package passed the race run.

hypotheses.title: CFG stage spawns one goroutine per function per analysis; each fresh 2KB stack is regrown by deep ast.Walk recursion
hypotheses.issue: Stage 8 (cfg.Analyze) runs its analyses concurrently, and each one starts a brand-new goroutine for every function, lambda and worker: analyzeReachability, analyzeExplicitReturn, analyzeUninitializedVars and analyzeFinalReassignments. Stage 7 (cfg.Build) does the same. Some of these per-function goroutines immediately do a full recursive ast.Walk over the function body: buildImplicitInitState looks only for foreach loop variables, and deferredFinalLocals looks only for final locals declared without an initializer. ast.Walk is a big type switch with a stack frame of about 920 bytes, so every new goroutine (starting at 2KB) goes through several runtime.newstack/copystack growths. The stacks are thrown away when the goroutine exits, so the same cost is paid again for the next function and the next analysis. In a CPU profile of the reproducer, runtime.newstack is about 21% of total CPU, about 75% of it under ast.Walk. Nearly all of the cost of buildImplicitInitState (about 1.3 s) and deferredFinalLocals (about 1.1 s) is stack growth rather than real work. Lock contention is negligible: this is about how finely the work is split. The same goroutine-per-function pattern also appears in types.ResolvePrivateNodes and desugar.DesugarPackage.

reproducer.command: python3 gen_repro.py 50000 many_small_fns.bal && go build -o bal ./cli/cmd && /usr/bin/time -f 'WALL %e U %U RSS %MKB' ./bal run --stats many_small_fns.bal 2>&1 >/dev/null | tail -15   # plus: ./bin/benchmark --mode time|memory --runs 5 --warmup 1 main <branch> many_small_fns.bal

hypotheses.fix_approach: The prototype adds a private helper, runParallel(tasks []func()), in semantics/internal/cfg/parallel.go. It starts min(GOMAXPROCS, len(tasks)) worker goroutines that take task indices from an atomic counter, so each worker keeps its already-grown stack across many functions. The goroutine-per-function loops in analyzeReachability, analyzeExplicitReturn, analyzeUninitializedVars, analyzeFinalReassignments and Build now collect closures into a task slice and call runParallel. Diagnostic order is unchanged: all goldens pass, because diagnostics were already order-independent of goroutine scheduling. Analyze itself still runs the analyses concurrently, so up to number-of-analyses x GOMAXPROCS goroutines exist at a time, which is fine. Further gains are possible: run all analyses of one function in one task, merge or avoid the two extra ast.Walk passes (the information could be collected during CFG build), and apply the same bounded pool in types.ResolvePrivateNodes and desugar.DesugarPackage. A shared helper in common/ could serve all of these.

notes: Other leads seen during exploration and not pursued: (1) loopTypeResolver/functionTypeResolver.compilerContext() and unnarrowedSymbol walk one parent per nesting level on every call, making 400 nested while loops or lambdas roughly cubic in Local Type Resolution (248 ms -> 1801 ms when depth doubles from 200 to 400); (2) CFG build creates a full semtypes.Context per function (control_flow_analyzer.go, about 2.3KB in 11 allocations) even though it is rarely used, while desugar already creates its context lazily; (3) nodebuilder.createBLangVarDef builds a BLangVariable, discards it and builds it again (about 1% of allocations).
